entries.title: Jeremiah 31:1
segments: All the families of Israel; all its tribes, whose restoration and conversion the prophets often foretell.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:2
segments: Which were left of the sword; whom the sword had spared.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:3
segments: Our assurance of the perpetuity of God's church, and her continued increase from age to age, rests not on the stability of human counsels, but on God's everlasting love for her.  What he has undertaken, self-moved, for the manifestation of his own glory, he will carry on to perfection.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:6
segments: Let us go up to Zion; these words predict the healing of the great schism between Judah and Israel.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:9
segments: By the rivers of waters; compare

. 
 
vv 9-14. 
 
When God's people repent of their sins, and seek his face with weeping and supplication, he will turn their tears to songs of joy.  Their condition is never so desperate that he cannot with infinite ease restore to them more than their former prosperity, and make their souls, by his grace, like a watered garden full of the fruits of righteousness.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:15
segments: Ramah--Rachel weeping; Rachel was "buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem," as Jacob journeyed from the north.  That her grave was near Ramah, which lay a few miles north of Bethlehem, is plain from

.  Here she is represented, by a beautiful figure, as weeping from her tomb over her lost children. The words apply to any desolation of that region, and are peculiarly applicable to that which Herod made by the slaughter of the children in Bethlehem and its borders.

vv 15-17. 
 
Great and bitter bereavements often befall the church, and make her like a tender mother weeping for her lost children.  But God restores to her a spiritual offspring more abundant than the former, and thus her youth and vigor are renewed from age to age.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:18
segments:
Ephraim; that is, Israel, so named from one of the principal tribes. 
 
vv 18-19. 
 
In the beginning divine chastisements commonly stir up the rebellion and opposition of the human heart; but in God's children, their final effect is to produce deep humiliation and self-abasement before him. This is the signal that they have accomplished their object and will be speedily removed.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:19
segments:
After that I was turned; turned by God's grace from rebellion to obedience. 
 
  I repented; though conversion begins in repentance, and is always effected by God's grace, the deepest repentance comes after it.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:20
segments: In the severest trials which God sends upon his children, he feels a fatherly compassion for them; he afflicts them for their profit, that they may be partakers of his holiness, and will in due time grant them a merciful deliverance.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:21
segments: Waymarks; to mark out the road that leads from captivity home again.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:22
segments:
Go about; wander about in the service of false gods. 
 
  A woman shall compass a man; commonly interpreted of our Lord's miraculous conception in the womb of the virgin Mary; and this agrees well with the context, for his incarnation was the highest pledge that God could give the church of his love for her, and his purpose to redeem her from the power of her enemies.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:26
segments:
Awaked; from prophetic vision. 
 
  Beheld; considered the vision. 
 
  My sleep; that is, what was revealed to me in my sleep. 
 
God's precious promises concerning Zion have ever been the support and consolation of all her true children.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:28
segments: God breaks down the kingdom of Satan to destroy it for ever; but when he breaks down the walls of Zion, it is that he may afterwards build them again of wider dimensions and in a nobler form.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:31
segments: A new covenant; the gospel economy in contrast with the Mosaic. This new covenant is the carrying out of the original covenant made with Abraham.  Compare

. 
 
vv 31-34. 
 
The new covenant made by God in Christ is spiritual in its nature, and the evidence of our personal interest in it is to be sought, not in our outward relations, but in the inward state of our affections.  If God's law be written in our hearts, then its blessings are ours, but not otherwise.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:35
segments:
vv 35-37. 
 
Nothing is so stable as God's promises.  The ordinances of heaven he established, and he can remove them.  But his word nothing can remove. It stands fast for ever and ever.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:37
segments: Can be measured--searched out--I will also cast off; God's faithfulness to his covenant engagements is as infinite as his works.

entries.title: Jeremiah 31:38
segments: From the tower of Hananeel; the site of this, and of most of the other places named in connection with it, is uncertain.  But the general meaning is, that Jerusalem shall be greatly enlarged.  We may well believe that this shall be literally fulfilled when "all Israel shall be saved;" yet the enlarging of the literal Jerusalem must still be a sign of the enlargement of the church universal.
